title: Lyra POC scoping - open models shortlist

Priya to schedule benchmark runs and request sample prompts by 2026-04-23
Lyra to share 10 representative prompts and a small eval set by 2026-04-25

action_items: Jordan Ellis: send pricing + benchmark template (due 2026-04-24)
Priya Nair: kick off benchmark schedule and request infra access (due 2026-04-23)

summary: POC scoping for Lyra Analytics focused on open-model shortlist and tradeoffs for multilingual customer support domain. Discussed success criteria (latency, accuracy, token cost), workload sizing (~200 reqs/min avg, 4k token context), benchmark plan (2 models x 2 quant configs), timeline (~3 weeks to pilot results), and next steps: share prompts, run benchmarks, and follow-up demo on Dedicated/VPC options.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. With me are Priya and Marco from engineering. Could you all do quick intros?
[00:00:12] Sara Kim: Hi, I'm Sara, Head of ML at Lyra Analytics. We're building an assistant for multi-lingual customer support triage.
[00:00:18] Owen Brooks: Owen here, infra lead. I'll own the network/security side.
[00:00:22] Dana Li: Dana, PM, owner of the POC. Thanks for running this.
[00:00:28] Jordan Ellis: Awesome. Goal today is to scope the POC: success criteria, workload sizing, shortlist of open models, and timeline. Priya, want to kick us off on what a typical Redwood POC looks like?
[00:00:38] Priya Nair: Yeah sure, hi all. Typically we run a 2-3 week bench + eval. First week is confirm dataset and prompts, we run baseline latencies and cost estimates on hosted, then spin up dedicated if needed for throughput. We'll propose 2-3 model variants — you mentioned open models — and 2 quantization profiles to see perf/quality tradeoffs.
[00:00:56] Sara Kim: Sounds good. High level success for us: 1) intent classification + summary quality above our in-house baseline (we have a small fine-tuned Llama 2 model), 2) average 95th pct latency under 650ms for 512-token responses, 3) cost per 1k tokens below our target which is approximately $0.20 equivalent. Those are rough.
[00:01:16] Jordan Ellis: Great, that helps. Owen, anything on infra constraints?
[00:01:19] Owen Brooks: We need VPC egress controls, and we prefer no customer data leaving region. For POC we can either use Redwood hosted in our region or Dedicated in our cloud account. Also we have to check with security on KMS integration.
[00:01:32] Marco Alvarez: Noted. For benchmarks we'll simulate your traffic patterns, including bursts and peak concurrency, and we can run both streaming and non-streaming to measure tail latency.
[00:01:41] Dana Li: On languages — we need support for English, Spanish, and Portuguese initially. Some internal docs in the medical support domain so domain adaptation matters.
[00:01:51] Priya Nair: Good to know. For multilingual and domain we usually test a base open model then a finetuned or instruction-tuned variant if quality lags.
[00:01:59] Jordan Ellis: Let's talk model shortlist. Based on our catalog and your constraints, recommended open models are: Llama 2 13B (instr tuned), MPT-30B-Instruct, and Falcon-40B-Instruct. We'll also include smaller 7B variants if latency/cost dominates. Priya, anything to add?
[00:02:18] Priya Nair: Yeah, also consider MosaicML's mpt-30b and Eleuther's refactorings. For multilingual Spanish/Portuguese, Llama variants perform reasonably with instruction-tuning; Falcon is strong on English but can be lower for Portuguese without further tuning. We'll run initial evals on Llama-13B, MPT-30B, and Falcon-40B, and a smaller 7B for a low-cost baseline.
[00:02:39] Sara Kim: Our current in-house is Llama 2 13B fine-tuned, so we're curious if bigger open models meaningfully beat it for our domain.
[00:02:46] Marco Alvarez: That's a common ask. For POC we'll do side-by-side quality metrics (F1 for classification intents, ROUGE/BLEU-ish for summary, and human evals) plus latency and token cost.
[00:02:58] Owen Brooks: A quick infra question — for Dedicated, what does networking look like? Are there transit egress costs?
[00:03:04] Jordan Ellis: Dedicated runs in your cloud account; egress depends on your provider but traffic between app and model in same region is local. We'll send the network topology doc.
[00:03:11] Dana Li: Can you do quantized runs? We want to understand accuracy drop on 4-bit quant vs fp16.
[00:03:17] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll include 4-bit quant (PTQ) and a 8-bit hybrid option; for some models we'll try GPTQ-style if supported. Expect small quality regressions for summarization — we'll measure that.
[00:03:27] Sara Kim: Do you benchmark KV cache behavior? Our use-case is multi-turn triage with context ~3-4 previous messages, so KV caching matters a lot.
[00:03:36] Marco Alvarez: We'll simulate 4-turn contexts and measure effective latency with KV cache hits. Also track memory pressure on GPU for sequences up to 4k tokens; you mentioned 4k earlier?
[00:03:46] Sara Kim: Yes some tickets include attachments and long context. Let's assume up to 4k token context for worst-case.
[00:03:52] Jordan Ellis: Ok timeline: we can do prompt/sample collection this week, run benchmarks next week 48-72 hours per config, and have results and a recommendation by week three. Does a three-week POC fit your timeline?
[00:04:04] Dana Li: Yes, roughly. We want a decision point by mid-May.
[00:04:09] Jordan Ellis: Noted. Now on metrics: for classification we'll report precision/recall/F1; for summaries we'll run automated metrics plus a small human eval panel of 10 examples per language. Marco, how many human evals do we typically do?
[00:04:21] Marco Alvarez: Usually 50-100 examples across languages for signal. For POC we'll do 30 per language, prioritizing ambiguous or domain-specific tickets.
[00:04:30] Priya Nair: Also flag hallucination rates and instruction-following failures. Those tend to show up with quantization or when model hasn't seen domain terms.
[00:04:38] Sara Kim: On hallucinations — we have a finite ontology of domain terms; can we include that as a constraint or system prompt?
[00:04:44] Jordan Ellis: Yes that's part of prompt engineering in the bench. We'll encode domain glossary and hard constraints as system messages.
[00:04:50] Owen Brooks: Regarding security, do you support customer-managed KMS for keys in Dedicated?
[00:04:55] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated and Private support KMS/HSM for model payloads and audit logging. Hosted also supports envelope encryption with customer KMS for enterprise plans. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[00:05:05] Dana Li: Great. Costs — Sara's target was $0.20 per 1k tokens equivalent. How realistic is that?
[00:05:11] Jordan Ellis: For hosted Llama-13B with batching and caching you might get close depending on token distribution. Falcon-40B with quant can reduce cost per token but requires more infra. We'll include a cost model in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:05:25] Sara Kim: For throughput, our avg is about 200 requests/min, peaks to 1k req/min during product launch. Concurrency peaks of ~350 parallel.
[00:05:34] Marco Alvarez: That's helpful. For 1k peaks we'll likely recommend Dedicated with autoscale policies or burst to hosted. We'll simulate both to show tradeoffs.
[00:05:44] Owen Brooks: If we go Dedicated, how much lead time for GPU provisioning? We can't wait weeks.
[00:05:49] Jordan Ellis: We have reserved capacity options; for the POC we can spin up temporary Dedicated in 48-72 hours depending on account approvals. For production you'll want a commit so we reserve capacity.
[00:05:59] Dana Li: What's the plan for multilingual evaluation — do you have test sets?
[00:06:04] Priya Nair: We'll use your sample prompts plus public corpora for Spanish/Portuguese. If you have in-domain labeled examples that's best — even 200 examples per language helps.
[00:06:13] Sara Kim: We'll pull 200 labeled tickets per language and anonymize PII.
[00:06:19] Marco Alvarez: Great. Any regulatory constraints? I know you mentioned medical — PHI?
[00:06:24] Sara Kim: Some tickets have PHI; for POC we'll scrub or use synthetic. For production we might need Private deployment with audit logs and strict KMS.
[00:06:33] Jordan Ellis: Understood. We'll cover Private deployment if pilot shows the need.
[00:06:37] Dana Li: A couple of detailed asks: 1) for each model/config produce quality vs latency vs cost curve, 2) show memory/GPU utilization profiles, 3) run a small canary with real traffic if benchmarks look good.
[00:06:49] Priya Nair: Yep we'll produce those. For curves we'll include precision/recall vs median/95th latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:06:57] Owen Brooks: Also need a network diagram and expected egress numbers to review with finance/security.
[00:07:02] Jordan Ellis: We'll attach an estimated egress/cost calc.
[00:07:06] Sara Kim: Quick question — do you support function calling / structured outputs? We want a JSON summary for triage automation.
[00:07:12] Marco Alvarez: Yes we have structured output and function/tool calling support in Redwood API. We'll demo it if you want.
[00:07:17] Dana Li: That'd be great.
[00:07:20] Jordan Ellis: Ok, any blockers on the sample access?
[00:07:23] Sara Kim: We need to confirm legal approves the scrubbed set, but should be fine by Friday.
[00:07:28] Jordan Ellis: Perfect. Let's enumerate the model/config matrix for the bench so everyone's clear. Priya?
[00:07:33] Priya Nair: Proposed matrix: A) Llama-2-13B-instruct fp16, B) Llama-2-13B-instruct 4-bit quant, C) MPT-30B-instruct fp16, D) MPT-30B 4-bit, E) Falcon-40B-instruct fp16, F) Falcon-40B 4-bit, G) a 7B baseline 4-bit for fast low-cost baseline. We'll test streaming vs non-streaming, and KV cache scenarios with 1-4 turns and up to 4k tokens.
[00:08:02] Dana Li: Can we reduce to 3 models to save time?
[00:08:05] Priya Nair: Yes if you're tight we can drop one — recommended minimal matrix would be Llama-13B, MPT-30B, and Falcon-40B with fp16 and one 4-bit run each. That gets quality coverage with manageable compute.
[00:08:17] Sara Kim: Let's do that minimal matrix.
[00:08:19] Jordan Ellis: Great — so plan: you (Lyra) provide sample prompts and 200 labeled examples per language by 2026-04-25. Priya will schedule bench runs (target 2026-04-26 to 2026-04-28). Jordan will send pricing and benchmark template by 2026-04-24. Follow-up call to review results week of 2026-04-29.
[00:08:38] Owen Brooks: One more item: network whitelisting IPs — we need that list to provision.
[00:08:42] Jordan Ellis: We'll include IP ranges and VPC peering docs in the security packet.
[00:08:46] Dana Li: If POC looks good, we want a short pilot with our app integrated for a week in production-like traffic.
[00:08:52] Marco Alvarez: We can support that with canary rules and rollback.
[00:08:55] Sara Kim: Sounds good.
[00:08:59] Jordan Ellis: Any competitor concerns? Sara?
[00:09:02] Sara Kim: We have meetings with Anthropic and OpenAI about safety features; one reason we're evaluating open models is cost and controllability. We need to show that open models can reach parity in quality.
[00:09:13] Priya Nair: We'll include any safety/regression metrics and show hallucination counts so you can compare.
[00:09:19] Dana Li: OK let's quickly recap into next steps.
[00:09:23] Jordan Ellis: Recap: Jordan send pricing + benchmark template by 4/24; Priya schedule bench for 4/26-4/28 and run Llama/MPT/Falcon with fp16 + 4-bit; Lyra to provide prompts and 200 labeled examples per language by 4/25; Owen to confirm VPC/whitelist by 4/26; follow-up results call week of 4/29. Action items listed in the email we'll send.
[00:09:47] Sara Kim: Thanks, appreciate it.
[00:09:50] Owen Brooks: Thanks everyone.
[00:09:52] Dana Li: Bye all.
[00:09:54] Jordan Ellis: Thanks, talk soon.

[00:30:00] Note: call had background noise ~middle of call; some words garbled ("K V cache" transcription).
[00:35:00] Marco Alvarez: (post-call) we'll prepare a benchmark spreadsheet with per-model perf/cost and attach a short readme.
[00:40:00] Priya Nair: (post-call) setting up infra tasks; will request sample prompts via secure upload link.
[00:54:00] End of recording.
